1.title: AWS Infrastructure and Services for GenAI
1.text: Welcome to Module six: A W S Infrastructure and Services for Gen A I. This module covers task statement two point three. You will learn which A W S services you use to build generative A I applications, why building on A W S has advantages, what the infrastructure gives you in security and compliance, and what the choices cost.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do four things. Identify the A W S services and features for generative A I: Bedrock, SageMaker A I, JumpStart, Quick, Kiro, Strands Agents and AgentCore. Describe the advantages of A W S generative A I services. Describe the benefits of A W S infrastructure: security, compliance, responsibility and safety. And describe the cost trade-offs: token pricing, provisioned throughput and custom models.

1.title: Case Check-In: Cedar and Salt Picks Its AWS Tools
1.text: Cedar and Salt Travel has a small team, and it wants generative A I fast, without running G P U servers. The engineers ask which A W S service gives them models, which one lets them customize, and which one runs agents. Finance asks what the options cost, and security asks who can see their data. Your job is to choose the right service for each need.

1.title: The AWS GenAI Services at a Glance
1.text: Here is the map of A W S generative A I services. The figure shows four layers. On top are tools for work and for developers: Amazon Quick, Kiro and A W S Transform. Next are the platforms: Amazon Bedrock for models as a service, SageMaker A I to build and customize, and AgentCore to run agents. Below are the models: Amazon Nova, other providers' models, and JumpStart models. And the foundation is A W S infrastructure, for security, compliance and scale. Exam tip: models through an A P I means Bedrock, building and tuning your own means SageMaker A I, and running agents means AgentCore.

1.title: Amazon Bedrock: Foundation Models as a Service
1.text: Amazon Bedrock is a fully managed service for secure access to foundation models from leading A I companies. You call one A P I, and there are no servers or G P Us to manage. It offers many providers, including Amazon, with tools to compare models on quality and cost. You can customize a model with your data, by R A G, fine-tuning or distillation. And you can build agents, add guardrails and evaluate results, all in one place. Exam tip: many models, one A P I and no infrastructure means Amazon Bedrock.

1.title: What Bedrock Adds Around the Model
1.text: Bedrock adds features around the model. Knowledge Bases connect a model to your documents for R A G; that is Module seven. Prompt Management stores and versions prompts; Module eight. Model customization covers fine-tuning, continued pre-training and distillation; Module nine. Model Evaluation compares models and settings; Module ten. Guardrails filter harmful input and output; Module eleven. And Agents and AgentCore build and run agents. Exam tip: match the feature to the need: grounding, prompts, tuning, testing, safety or agents.

1.title: Amazon Nova
1.text: Amazon Nova is A W S's own portfolio of A I offerings. Nova models are fast, cost-effective foundation models for text and multi-modal needs, including speech. Nova Forge is a service to build your own frontier models using Nova. And Nova Act is a service for agents that automate browser-based workflows. As of the fifth of November, twenty twenty-six, model names and versions change quickly, so check the Nova page. Exam tip: Nova is the family of Amazon-built foundation models.

1.title: Amazon SageMaker AI and SageMaker JumpStart
1.text: SageMaker A I builds, trains and deploys M L and foundation models, with managed infrastructure. SageMaker JumpStart is a hub of pretrained, open-source models and solution templates. From JumpStart you can deploy, fine-tune and evaluate a model. You choose the instances, the training settings and the hosting, which means more control and more to manage. And reviewing the license of a third-party model is your responsibility. Exam tip: pretrained models to deploy or fine-tune yourself mean SageMaker JumpStart.

1.title: Bedrock or SageMaker AI?
1.text: How do you choose between them? For the fastest start, with one A P I and no infrastructure: Amazon Bedrock. To compare several providers' models: Amazon Bedrock. For full control of training, instances and hosting: SageMaker A I. To deploy and tune an open-source model yourself: SageMaker JumpStart. And for custom M L models beyond foundation models: SageMaker A I. Exam tip: least effort means Bedrock, and most control means SageMaker A I.

1.title: Amazon Quick, Kiro and AWS Transform
1.text: Three more tools appear in the guide. Amazon Quick is an A I companion for work: research, business insights and automation, for business users. Kiro is an A I-powered development environment, with specs, steering and M C P tools, for developers. A W S Transform is agentic A I that speeds up the migration and modernization of servers, applications and code, for I T teams. As of the fifth of November, twenty twenty-six, these products change fast, so confirm details on the A W S pages. Exam tip: ready-made A I for people at work is Quick, for developers it is Kiro, and for modernizing workloads it is A W S Transform.

1.title: Strands Agents and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
1.text: Two services help with agents. Strands Agents is an S D K to build and run agents in your own code, with tools, M C P support and multi-agent patterns. Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is a platform to deploy and operate agents securely at scale, with any framework and any model. Its parts include Runtime, Memory, Gateway, Identity, Observability and Policy. As of the fifth of November, twenty twenty-six, the AgentCore service list keeps growing. Exam tip: building an agent in code means Strands Agents, and running and governing agents at scale means AgentCore.

1.title: Advantages of Building GenAI on AWS
1.text: What are the advantages of building generative A I on A W S? Accessibility and a lower barrier to entry: you use models through an A P I, without M L expertise. Efficiency and speed to market: ready-made services shorten the path from idea to product. Cost-effectiveness: you pay per use instead of buying G P Us. Business fit: many models and tools, so you can meet your own business objectives. And scale and security are built in. Exam tip: A P I access, no G P U purchase and fast to market are the advantages of A W S generative A I services.

2.title: Benefits of AWS Infrastructure for GenAI
2.text: A W S infrastructure brings four kinds of benefit. Security: data is encrypted in transit and at rest, access is controlled with I A M, and V P C and PrivateLink keep traffic private. Compliance: A W S lists programs such as I S O, S O C, G D P R and H I P A A eligibility. Responsibility and safety: Guardrails, evaluation and monitoring help keep output safe. Model providers have no access to Bedrock logs, or to your prompts and completions. Under shared responsibility, you still manage access and your data. As of the fifth of November, twenty twenty-six, details are on the Amazon Bedrock security pages. Exam tip: A W S secures the platform, and you control who can use it and which data goes in.

2.title: Cost Trade-Offs of AWS GenAI Services
2.text: Every choice has a cost trade-off. On-demand tokens let you pay per token, only for use, but cost rises with the length of prompts and answers. Batch inference gives a discount for jobs that can wait, but it is not for real-time answers. Provisioned Throughput gives steady performance and responsiveness with reserved capacity, but it is a commitment, paid even when idle. Custom models fit your domain better, but add training and storage charges. And region and redundancy choices bring availability and coverage near users, with Amazon CloudFront delivering content from edge locations, but extra copies and traffic cost more. Track spend with A W S Budgets alerts and Cost Explorer analysis. Exam tip: spiky use means on-demand, steady heavy use means provisioned, and jobs that can wait mean batch.

2.title: What the Exam Asks: AWS Services for GenAI
2.text: Here is how the exam frames this module. Which service: Bedrock, SageMaker A I, JumpStart, Quick, Kiro, Strands Agents or AgentCore. Which advantage: accessibility, a lower barrier, speed to market or cost-effectiveness. Which benefit: security, compliance, responsibility or safety. Which cost choice: on-demand tokens, batch, provisioned throughput or a custom model. And which tool for cost: A W S Budgets or Cost Explorer. Exam tip: name the need first, then the service.

2.title: Design Check: Cedar and Salt's AWS Stack
2.text: Now a design check. Cover the right column and choose. Models from several providers through one A P I: Amazon Bedrock. Deploy and tune an open-source model with full control: SageMaker JumpStart and SageMaker A I. Research and insights for the leadership team: Amazon Quick. An A I development environment for engineers: Kiro. A framework to code a booking agent: Strands Agents. Run and govern agents securely at scale: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Cheaper overnight review summaries: batch inference. And an alert when generative A I spend passes a limit: A W S Budgets. Pause the video if you want more time.

2.title: Try It: Compare Two Models in the Bedrock Playground (Optional)
2.text: This is an optional hands-on slide, for a practice account. The goal is to see that models differ in quality, speed and cost. Open Amazon Bedrock in the console, and if it asks, follow the steps to get access to two models. Open the chat playground and send the same review-summary prompt to each model. Compare the answers, the response time and the token counts shown. Then switch to another model and repeat, and note which one meets your quality bar at the lowest cost. Nothing is left running; the playground bills only for the tokens you use. Exam tip: hands-on work is not tested on this exam, but it makes model trade-offs concrete.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. The services: Bedrock for models as a service, SageMaker A I and JumpStart to build and tune, Quick, Kiro and A W S Transform as tools, and Strands Agents and AgentCore for agents. The advantages: accessibility, a lower barrier, efficiency, speed to market and cost-effectiveness. The infrastructure gives security, compliance, responsibility and safety, under shared responsibility. And the cost choices are on-demand tokens, batch, provisioned throughput and custom models, with Budgets and Cost Explorer to track them.

2.title: Practice Question 1
2.text: Question one. Cedar and Salt wants to try foundation models from several providers through one A P I, without managing servers. Which service fits best? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B, Amazon Bedrock. It gives secure access to foundation models from many providers through one A P I, with no infrastructure to manage. SageMaker A I means managing training and hosting, and Rekognition and Polly are task-specific services.

2.title: Practice Question 2
2.text: Question two. The data science team wants to deploy a pretrained open-source model and fine-tune it, with full control over instances and hosting. Which A W S option fits best? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D, Amazon SageMaker JumpStart. It offers pretrained open-source models that you can deploy, fine-tune and evaluate with SageMaker A I, giving full control over instances and hosting. The other options do not provide or tune models.

2.title: Practice Question 3
2.text: Question three. Select two. Which two are advantages of building generative A I applications with A W S managed services? The five options are on the screen. The answers are A and C. Managed services lower the barrier to entry and shorten the time to market. They do not guarantee correct output, they do not remove the need to evaluate and monitor, and under shared responsibility customers still manage access and data.

2.title: Practice Question 4
2.text: Question four. Which A W S offering is a platform to deploy and operate A I agents securely at scale, with any framework and any model? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. It is an agentic platform for building, deploying and operating agents securely at scale, with services such as Runtime, Memory, Gateway, Identity and Observability. The other services do different jobs.

2.title: Practice Question 5
2.text: Question five. Cedar and Salt's busy season brings steady, heavy traffic to its assistant, and it needs reliable throughput. Which pricing option fits best? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A, Provisioned Throughput. It reserves capacity per model unit for a commitment term, so it suits steady, high-volume workloads that need reliable performance. Batch results arrive later, and on-demand pricing has no capacity commitment.

2.title: Practice Question 6
2.text: Question six. Finance wants an alert when monthly generative A I spending passes a set amount. Which service helps? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B, A W S Budgets. It tracks spending against a threshold and sends alerts, and Cost Explorer analyzes where the money went. Artifact, CloudFront and Config do not warn about spending.

2.title: Answers at a Glance
2.text: Here are all six answers. Question one: B. Question two: D. Question three: A and C. Question four: C. Question five: A. Question six: B. That completes Module six, and the second domain. Next, Module seven opens the domain on applications of foundation models, with design considerations: choosing a model, inference parameters, retrieval augmented generation and agents.
